text:
anna: Heads-up — our batching telemetry is pretty sparse. Last week's perf regression was painful to debug because we couldn't correlate batch utilization, queue depth, and tokens/sec per model/hardware. We should add a dedicated dashboard and a few new metrics.

raj: +1. Can you sketch what panels/metrics you want? I can wire the exporters once we decide names/labels.

anna: quick sketch:
- timeseries: batch_utilization (actual tokens processed / batch_capacity) per model, per host
- heatmap: batch_size distribution over time (0..N), split by model family
- timeseries: queue_depth and queue_wait_seconds (p50/p95)
- timeseries: tokens_per_second (in/out), separate for requests served from KV vs cold
- gauge: kernel_variant chosen (label), and op_latency for key kernels (matmul, softmax)
- gauge: redwood.kv.cache_hit_ratio per model + per-tenant

marcus: love it. Metric name suggestions so prometheus + grafana are straightforward:
```
redwood_batch_utilization{model="gptj-6b",host="gpu-12"}
redwood_batch_size{model=...,host=...}
redwood_queue_depth{queue="continuous_batcher",model=...}
redwood_queue_wait_seconds_bucket{le=...,model=...}
redwood_tokens_in_per_sec{model=...,kv="hit|miss"}
redwood_kernel_variant{kernel="fused_attention",variant="v2"}
redwood_kernel_op_latency_seconds_sum{op="matmul"}
redwood_kv_cache_hit_ratio{model=...,tenant=...}
```

sophie: A couple of policy notes from heuristic tuning side:
- We need to surface "tokens_per_batch_target" as a metric so we can correlate when the heuristic reduces/increases the target and how it affects latency SLOs.
- Also emit "batch_formation_reason" label (e.g., target_full, timeout, kv_miss) so dashboards can filter by why batches close.

jordan: aggregation question — should dashboards default to per-host and have an overall cluster rollup? Per-tenant is useful for Dedicated customers.

raj: yes — label strategy: host, model, tenant(optional), kernel_arch, and batcher_type. Grafana vars will let folks pivot. We'll keep cluster rollups as sum/avg with proper cardinality guards.

anna: alerting proposals:
- queue_depth (per model) > 50 for > 3m -> P1 paging (indicates backlog)
- batch_utilization < 0.2 for > 5m -> warn (implies inefficient small batches)
- tokens_in_per_sec drops > 30% vs baseline for a model -> trigger investigation (could be KV or kernel regression)

marcus: Add a regression hook: emit current kernel_variant + commit_hash when we change kernels. Then link to recent kernel perf histograms. That made last regression easy to trace.

sophie: Implementation note: the continuous batcher already tracks internal counters; we can add atomic counters for tokens_queued, tokens_flushed, batches_closed_by_reason. Each minor change should be cheap. I can PR the instrumentation.

raj: example prometheus queries for panels:
```
# batch utilization p50/p95
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_batch_utilization_bucket[5m])) by (le, model))

# current queue depth per model
sum(redwood_queue_depth) by (model)

# tokens/sec split by kv hit/miss
sum(rate(redwood_tokens_in_total[1m])) by (model, kv)
```

anna: great. Also add a small panel that shows avg queue_wait_seconds broken down by batch_formation_reason — that will help tune timeouts vs token targets.

marcus: KV impacts batching a lot. When cache hits are high we often see larger batch sizes and higher tokens/sec; when misses spike we see many small batches. Suggest a Grafana composite: top: kv_cache_hit_ratio, middle: batch_size histogram, bottom: tokens/sec.

perf-bot: Incident inc-2025-04-batching: last regression correlated with kernel_variant=v1->v2 swap and a change in default tokens_per_batch_target. Logs attached in incident ticket.

anna: linking the perf regression here is perfect — we should add a panel that overlays kernel_variant changes on timeseries (annotation layer).

sophie: ops question — do we throttle metrics emission frequency for high QPS hosts? We should sample histograms at 1s buckets but aggregate before export.

raj: yes, local aggregation on the host, push to prometheus pushgateway or remote_write with sane cardinality. We'll cap label cardinality for tenant to top N and use rollups for rest.

jordan: owner/next steps?

anna: Sophie will open the instrumentation PR for the batcher + kv labels (ETA 2d). Marcus will add kernel_variant commit hash in runtime (ETA 3d). Raj will sketch Grafana dashboard JSON + alert rules (ETA EOD). I'll create an incident playbook snippet for when queue_depth spikes.

marcus: I'll also add a small perf test to our CI to simulate kv miss/hit patterns and assert tokens/sec doesn't drop >20% between variants.

sophie: I'll ping once the PR is up for review and include a sample payload + expected metric outputs.

anna: thanks all. Once dashboards exist we'll run a 48h observability spike and then iterate on the heuristic tuning. :rocket:
